items.text: For thousands of years, chocolate has attracted humans. However, its production links to widespread deforestation, slave labor, and child labor. Five to ten companies dominate 90% of the cacao and chocolate markets, and for the last 60 years, these companies supported these malpractices . WNWN Food Labs is a company with a mission to create an ethical version of chocolate, and it makes surprisingly tasty imitation treats. The company wants to accelerate change, raise consumer awareness, and recognize that mass-market chocolate doesn’t need cocoa, and alternative ingredients can taste even better. Instead of cacao beans, the process uses other plant-based matter, for example, barley or legumes. These ingredients are fermented, roasted, mixed with some powders, liquids, and sugar to get a substance very similar to conventional chocolate. WNWN wants to create a sustainable version of chocolate that tastes the same but uses local and regional ingredients and producers. The company wants to focus on other ingredients like coffee, tea, and vanilla, too. Difficult words: malpractice (illegal or unprofessional behavior), imitation (a thing that copies something else), conventional (ordinary or widely accepted). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Only a few companies dominate the cacao and chocolate markets, and for the last 60 years, these companies supported deforestation and child labor . West Africa creates over 70% of the world’s chocolate. People can only grow cacao near the equator, and climate change is changing how people can grow cacao. Company WNWN Food Labs wants to make chocolate from only local or regional ingredients. The process uses barley or legumes instead of cocoa beans, but the final product looks and tastes like real chocolate. The company wants to make customers aware of problems in the chocolate industry, and it wants to focus on coffee, tea, and vanilla, too. Difficult words: dominate (to control or have power over someone or something), deforestation (cut and remove trees in large areas), child labor (the illegal work of children), legume (peas, beans, and similar seeds). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A few companies run the cacao and chocolate markets. Cacao only grows near the middle of the Earth. West Africa makes most of the world’s chocolate. Chocolate companies are responsible for a lot of dirty areas and deforestation . Children often work on big cocoa farms. Child work is illegal. Many people eat chocolate. They do not know about these problems. WNWN Food Labs is a British company. It makes fake chocolate. This chocolate looks and tastes like real chocolate. The process doesn’t use cocoa beans. It uses barley or legumes instead. They also use local ingredients. They are better for the natural world. Difficult words: deforestation (when people cut down many trees), barley (a grain to make food, beer, and alcohol), legume (peas, beans and similar seeds). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In an effort to reduce the spread of sexually transmitted diseases, young people in France will get condoms free of charge from next year. On Thursday, French president Emmanuel Macron said that condoms would be free in drugstores for those aged 18 to 25. He added that France faced challenges in sexual education. According to health authorities, the rate of sexually transmitted diseases increased by about 30% in 2020 and 2021 in the country. In 2008, the French government started to reimburse the cost of condoms to individuals if they purchased them in a drugstore with a prescription from a doctor or midwife . Earlier this year, the government made contraception free for all women up to 26 years old. Contraception was previously free for women and girls 18 or younger. Difficult words: reimburse (to repay), prescription (a written order to give permission to get a drug), midwife (a person who assists women in childbirth). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Thursday, French president Emmanuel Macron said that people between the age 18 to 25 would get condoms for free. Macron said that France had big problems with sexual education. Since 2018, the French can get free condoms if they buy them in a drugstore with a prescription from a doctor. Then health officials reported that there was a 30% increase in sexually transmitted diseases since 2020. Since this year, contraception in France is free for all women up to 26 years old, which will have an impact on millions of women. Previously, only young women up to 18 years old could get contraception for free. Difficult words: prescription (a piece of paper from a doctor to get a drug in a drugstore), sexually transmitted disease (a disease which gets from one person to another when they have sex together), contraception (drugs or surgery that stop a woman from pregnancy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

France has a problem with sexually transmitted diseases. These diseases happen when people have sex. Since 2020, these diseases happen more often. The French president says that the sexual education is very bad in France. Since 2018, the French can get free condoms in a drugstore . They must have written permission from a doctor. This situation will change next year. All people between 18 to 25 years old will get free condoms. Another important change happens with contraception. Contraception is pills or surgeries which stop a woman from pregnancy . Since this year, contraception is free for all women up to 26 years old. Difficult words: sexual education (when children or young people get information about sex and relationships), drugstore (a shop where you can buy medicines, make up, and other things), pregnancy (when a woman’s body has a baby inside). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two women sued Apple; they said their former partners used the company’s AirTag devices to track their whereabouts . An AirTag is a small tracking device, slightly larger than a coin. People can attach it to keys, wallets, or backpack to locate lost items. However, privacy experts and police say that some people have used them for criminal and malicious purposes, such as to stalk. The women called AirTags the weapon of choice of stalkers and abusers, and they say that the device has been linked to several murders this year. One of the women said that her ex-boyfriend placed the device into the wheel of a tire on her car, and he disguised it with a sharpie marker . Apple didn’t immediately respond to the lawsuit; however, earlier this year, the company added more safeguards to the device to reduce unwanted tracking. Difficult words: whereabouts (the place where a person or thing is), sharpie marker (a type of marker with long lasting ink), safeguard (a type of protection). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

An AirTag is a small device; it is only a little larger than a coin. We can attach it to keys, wallets, or backpacks, and it locates things when we can’t find them. Some people use it in a way which is dangerous or which can hurt others. Two American women are suing Apple, the company which makes AirTag. They say that the device helps stalkers . One of the women said that her ex-boyfriend put AirTag on the tire of her car, so that he knew where she was. Police said that some murders happened this year in which Air Tag played a part. Earlier this year, Apple changed the device to make it safer and less easy for stalkers to use it. Difficult words: locate (to find where something is), sue (to take legal action against a person or organization), stalker (a person who illegally follows and watches someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An AirTag is a tracking device . A tracking device helps people find things. You can attach AirTag to your keys, wallet, or other things. The company Apple makes AirTag. Now, two women are suing Apple. The women say that AirTag is dangerous. Some people can use it in a bad way. An example is a stalker. This person follows, watches, or calls someone repeatedly . One of the women says that her ex-boyfriend puts Air Tag on her car. Then he can always know where she is. Police say that some women already die because of AirTag this year. Difficult words: device (a thing which people use for a specific task), sue (to take legal action against a person or organization), repeatedly (again and again). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Saturday, hundreds of people gathered at the foothills of Mount Kilimanjaro for the Maasai Olympics. The event is an alternative rite of passage to protect wildlife, and conservationists promote it. It has a great benefit to the community because young men focus on physical training to win medals and prize money instead of lion hunts. They compete in games including spear throw, athletics, and high jump. In Kenya, around 2,000 lions remain, and the biggest threat to them and other carnivores is human conflicts. To curb the practice of killing lions, Maasai cultural leaders worked with conservationists to create the Maasai Olympics. According to them, the program has had a huge impact on the lion population. Kenya is one of the few areas in Africa outside of protected areas where the lion population is stable or growing. Difficult words: rite of passage (a ceremony that marks an important stage in someone’s life), spear (a weapon you throw with a sharp blade), curb (to control or limit something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Saturday, hundreds of people competed in Kenya in the Maasai Olympics. Young men competed in spear throw, athletics, high jump, and other sports. Maasai leaders and conservationists wanted to protect animals. Instead of lion and other animal hunts, young Maasai men train for the Olympics to win medals and money. The event is becoming more popular among young Maasai, and it is an important ritual for them. Maasai Olympics reduce the hunt of animals. With around 2,000 lions, Kenya is only one of a few places where the lion population is not falling. Difficult words: spear (a long weapon with a sharp end), conservationist (a person who works to protect the natural world), ritual (a formal ceremony). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last week, the Maasai Olympics happen in Kenya. Spear throw, athletics, and high jump are among the disciplines . The event is very important. Around 2,000 lions live in Kenya. The biggest problem for lions is conflict with people. Conservationists are people who work to protect the natural world. They speak with Maasai leaders to save lions in Kenya. They decide on the Olympics. Young Maasai men train for the Olympics. They do not kill lions and other animals. Now, more lions are living in Kenya. It is one of the few places in Africa. Difficult words: spear (a long weapon with a sharp end), discipline (a type of sport or physical activity), conflict (a fight or serious problem). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Wednesday, the German police arrested 25 people on suspicion of a plan to overthrow the government and seize power in a violent far-right coup. The arrests happened during raids across the country, and more than 3,000 police and security forces took part from 11 German states. The suspects included active military members and people with links to extremist conspiracy groups ; these groups don’t recognize the legitimacy of modern day Germany. They insist that the larger Deutsche Reich still exists despite the Nazi’s defeat in World War II. Police suspect the plotters of actual plans to storm the German federal parliament with a small armed group. The plotters focused on recruiting military members and police officers as they hoarded military hardware and holding drills. Local police also arrested suspects in Austria and Italy. Difficult words: conspiracy group (people who secretly plan to do something unlawful or harmful), legitimacy (the fact that something is legal), hoard (to store things and hide them). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Wednesday, more than 3,000 police officers raided places across Germany. They arrested 25 people and accused them of a plan to overthrow the government. The people planned to attack the German parliament after November 2021. Among the arrested people were soldiers, a politician, a judge, and people in extremist groups . Some of the people believed that Nazi Germany still existed, although Nazi Germany ended after World War II. The group collected military equipment and held military trainings to get new people. Police also arrested several people in Austria and Italy. Difficult words: raid (to attack suddenly), overthrow (to remove someone from power by force), extremist group (people with strong opinions who want to change the political situation in a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Wednesday, 3,000 police officers arrest 25 people across Germany. These people plan to overthrow the government. Some arrested people are soldiers, a politician, a judge, and people from extremist groups . They plan to attack the German parliament. They plan since November 2021. Some of these people believe that Nazi Germany still exists. They do not believe that Nazi Germany ends after World War II. They do not accept today’s Germany. The group gets new members . They get special training. Police also arrest several people in Austria and Germany. Difficult words: overthrow (to end a government by force), extremist group (people with strong ideas who want to change the government in a country), member (someone who belongs to a group or organization). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2001, Toshiyuki Inoko started teamLab as an art collective, a place for various experts to experiment. The experts range from international artists, architects, programmers, and mathematicians; they seek to navigate the convergence of art, science, technology, and the natural world. To explore the idea to be unconstrained , Toshiyuki opened the world’s first digital art museum in Tokyo, Japan, called teamLab Borderless. From experimentation with interactive installations to steps into water, teamLab has wowed people all over the world in more than 50 cities. One of the museums is in a forest in southern Japan, and according to Toshiyuki, people can feel the long continuity of life through various artworks. Digital technology has made it possible for artworks to expand physically, and thus, viewers experience the artwork much more directly. Digital technology can also turn nature into art without harm. Difficult words: convergence (two or more things or ideas together and form a new whole), u nconstrain (to not be restricted), installation (an art exhibit in a museum or gallery). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2001, Toshiyuki Inoko and four of his friends started an art collective called teamLab. An art collective is a group of artists who work together to create artwork. People who work in teamLab are artists, architects, programmers, and mathematicians, and they want to connect art, science, and the natural world to create artwork. With the help of digital technology, they want to show people that art has no limits . In 2018, teamLab opened the world’s first digital art museum in Tokyo, and since then, the artists held exhibitions in all the world. Toshiyuki said that digital technology gives a greater experience to visitors. In a forest in Japan, visitors feel the continuity of life, and they wander in a dreamy world and not hurt nature. Difficult words: limit (how far something can go), continuity (a situation when something continues over time), wander (to walk or more around slowly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Toshiyuki Inoko is an artist. In 2001, he and his four friends start teamLab. TeamLab is a group of artists. They work together to make art. Other people work in teamLab, too. They are architects, programmers , and mathematicians. They put together art, science, and the natural world. They create amazing works of art. They show that art has no stop. Everything is possible with the help of digital technology. In 2018, TeamLab opens the first digital art museum in the world. The museum is in Tokyo. Visitors can see interactive art. They walk in water. Another museum is in a forest in Japan. Visitors walk through a forest. The place looks like a dream. Difficult words: programmer (a person who writes computer programs), digital (technology that is inside electronic devices), interactive (when a computer reacts with a person). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

West African leaders said they would establish a regional peacekeeping force to restore regional security and constitutional order . Although West and Central Africa have made steps to change their reputations as a ‘coup belt’, the region witnessed several coups in the past two years. The Economic Commission for West African States, ECOWAS, wants to boost constitutional governments in its member states. On December 4, 2022, ECOWAS leaders met at an annual summit in Nigeria’s capital, Abuja. They didn’t give any details of what would constitute the force; however, they said that they would meet next month to establish the force’s operations. They also expressed concern over the continued detention of 46 Ivorian soldiers in Mali, and they asked Malian authorities to release them by the end of this month. Difficult words: constitutional order (the laws and rules of a country’s constitution which most people follow), reputation (the general beliefs or opinions), constitute (to establish by law). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

ECOWAS is a political and economic union of 15 West African countries. In 1975, the countries created it with its main goal of regional independence. On December 4, 2022, leaders of ECOWAS met in Abuja, Nigeria. They established a special force to keep regional peace . In the past two years, many coups happened in the region, and the leaders wanted change. They wanted to support local governments and fight against militants. The leaders also asked Malian authorities to release 46 Ivorian soldiers by the end of December. Police arrested the soldiers in Mali’s capital in July, which started a diplomatic conflict between Mali and its West African neighbors. Difficult words: peace (the time when no war happens), coup (a quick and violent change of government), diplomatic conflict (a fight when two or more countries have problems with each other). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 1975, 15 West African countries make a group. It is called ECOWAS. These countries to work in business and politics. Recently, several coups happen in these countries. The situation in some countries is not safe. On December 4, 2022, ECOWAS leaders meet in Nigeria. They speak about security in West Africa. They want to make the area safer. In July, police in Mali arrest 46 Ivorian soldiers. Since that time, ECOWAS and Mali have a bad relationship with each other. ECOWAS leaders say that Mali must free the soldiers by the end of December. Difficult words: coup (a sudden and dangerous change in government (, security (safety), relationship (two or more things or people are connected). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Homosexuality is illegal in 69 countries, and in many, it leads to long prison sentences and the death penalty by public stoning or hanging. Many of these countries are very religious, and families and communities reject homosexual and transgender people for being against their faith. However, in Yogykarta, Indonesia, a majority Muslim country, a boarding school exists for transgender women. Shinta Ratri founded the school 14 years ago. As a transgender woman, she believed a safe place was essential for these women. Ratri risked her life to save others, and she plans to continue her fight. The Al-Fatah Islamic School has over 60 students, and it maintains the country’s Islamic values. According to some women, their main struggles are understanding both their faith and their identity. Difficult words: stoning (punishment by throwing stones), boarding school (a school where students live and study). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

14 years ago, Shinta Ratri founded a boarding school in Yogykarta, Indonesia. As a transgender woman, she wanted to create a place where other transgender women would feel safe. Homosexuality is illegal in 69 countries, and many of these countries are very religious. Families don’t want to be with homosexual and transgender people because to them, these people are not religious enough. Homosexual and transgender people may get life in prison or public stoning or hanging. Over 60 women are at the school, and Ratri probably saved their lives. She says that she will continue her work to protect transgender women. For some of the women, they struggle to understand their religion and their identity at the same time. Difficult words: boarding school (a school where students live and study), public stoning (a punishment when a group of people throw stones at someone to kill them), identity (to know who or what someone or something is). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A homosexual is a man who likes men. A homosexual is also, a woman who likes women. A transgender is a man who feels he is a woman. A transgender is also a woman who feels she is a man. Homosexuality is against the law in 69 countries. Many of these countries are very religious . Families do not spend time with homosexual or transgender people. They say that these people are not religious enough. Homosexual people often go to prison for many years. Some die. Their government public ly stones or hangs them. 14 years ago, Shinta Ratri starts a school for transgender women in Indonesia. She saves these women. More than 60 women study at the school. The women have a hard time to know who they are. They are religious people. They also have their sexual identity . Difficult words: religious (people who believe in a god and who follow traditional laws), public ly stone (to throw stones at someone, and this person dies), sexual identity (if someone feels like he is a man or a woman, and if this person likes men or women). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Astronauts Josh Cassada and Frank Rubio ventured into space for the longest spacewalk in both astronauts’ careers. In an operation that took seven hours, the NASA astronauts delivered six new solar arrays for for the International Space Station (ISS). Space X’s Dragon cargo craft delivered the array on November 27, 2022, and it’ll provide the ISS with up to 30% more power. According to NASA, it’ll create a total of 120 kilowatts of energy during orbital daytim e to support the station operations and scientific research. Out of six to install, these solar arrays are the third and fourth. Overall, they will increase the station’s total available power to up to 215 kilowatts. Difficult words: venture (to undertake an exciting or risky journey), array (an arrangement of things of a similar kind), orbital daytime (the length of day for a thing rotating around Earth) You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Astronauts Josh Cassada and Frank Rubio went for a spacewalk. The walk lasted more than 7 hours, and for both men, it was the longest spacewalk in their lives. The astronauts traveled to the International Space Station in November 2022 to repair the station’s solar panels. The plan is to install six arrays of panels, and the astronauts recently installed the third and fourth ones. The new panels will increase the station’s power by 30%, which is important for the station’s operations and scientific research. According to NASA, the station’s total power will be up to 215 kilowatts . Difficult words: array (a group of similar things), total (the whole number or amount of something), kilowatt (a measurement of electrical power). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two NASA astronauts go for a spacewalk. A spacewalk is work outside the spaceship. They spend more than 7 hours in open space . The astronauts travel to the International Space Station in November 2022. Their job is to fix the station’s solar panels. The astronauts put in new panels. These panels will grow the station’s power by a lot. Astronauts will put in six new sets of solar panels. The panels will make 215 kilowatts of power. The International Space Station needs more power for its operations and research. Difficult words: open space (the area outside the spaceship; it is dangerous because a lot of gravity and objects are in space), kilowatt (an amount of electrical power), operation (work or active). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Baker Stéphane Grattier presented French president Emmanuel Macron with a baguette while Macron spoke at the French Embassy in Washington, USA. The United Nations added the French baguette to the list of intangible cultural heritage as a cherished tradition that humanity should preserve. Last week, UNESCO experts gathered in Morocco, and they decided that the simple French flute made from flour, water, salt and yeast deserved UN recognition. With the bread’s new status, the French government plans to start an artisanal baguette day. Although France produces around 16 million baguettes a day, France’s culture ministry warned of a continuous decline in the number of traditional bakeries. Almost 400 bakeries have closed every year over the past half-century. Difficult words: intangible cultural heritage (unable to see or feel the history or traditions of a culture), cherish (protect and care for someone of something), artisanal (traditional method by someone skilled with his hands). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last week, UNESCO added the French baguette to the list of cultural heritage . France makes around 16 million baguettes every day, but the number of traditional French bakeries is dropping. Every year, around 400 bakeries close, and the French government hopes that with the new status , the baguette will become popular again. The government plans to create a baguette day to make the French proud of their traditional product. French president Emmanuel Macron visited the French Embassy in the United States last week. He was very excited about the news, and he said that the French baguette was more than just a piece of bread. Macron said that the baguette represented the bakers and the future for French children. Difficult words: cultural heritage (things or buildings which people get from past generations), traditional (something that people do for a long time without change), status (an official position). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The French baguette is very popular. The baguette is a long type of bread. France makes around 16 million baguettes every day. Recently, French bakeries close. Every year, more than 400 of them close. The French government wants to do something about the situation. For a long time, the country wants the baguette to be on a global list. The global list is for UNESCO and cultural heritage . The list explains things that must last for the next generations . Last week, UNESCO experts put the French baguette on the list. The French government will make a baguette day. This day will make the French people proud of the product . Difficult words: heritage (culture, languages, buildings, and other things which we get from people who live before us), generation (all the people who live at about the same time), product (something that people make and sell). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Medical experts applauded the results of a study; the study followed an experimental Alzheimer’s drug called Lecanemab. The phase 3 study spanned 18 months, and it enrolled nearly 1,800 participants with early-stage Alzheimer’s. According to the results, the drug slowed cognitive decline in some patients, which some experts said was amazing. This trial was the first to show clear and positive results because the drug lowered amyloid plaque amounts. These proteins play a key role in Alzheimer’s disease. However, the drug may carry a risk of serious side effects. Nearly 13% of patients in the trial experienced a dangerous type of brain swelling, and some also experienced bleeding in the brain. These side effects are serious, but experts suggest that they do not frequently occur, and they MRI scans can monitor them. Difficult words: phase 3 study (a study to see if a specific treatment helps a specific group of people), cognitive (relating to thinking or remembering), MRI scan (a medical imaging technique that uses radio waves, a magnet, and a computer to create pictures of the organs in the body). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Researchers tested a new drug called Lecanemab; it could slow down Alzheimer’s Disease. Some of the brain’s proteins are responsible for the disease; the drug reduced some of them. The result excited experts because it has never happened before. The study lasted 18 months, and it involved 1,800 patients. Unfortunately, some of the patients experienced serious side effects such as brain swelling or bleeding . Experts believed that these problems could be easily monitored with the help of special x-rays . They said that the new drug would change the lives of patients with Alzheimer’s. Difficult words: swell (to become larger or rounder), bleed (to lose blood from the body), protein (a piece of a tiny body part called a cell). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Alzheimer’s is a serious disease. It changes thoughts and memories. Researchers test a new drug. They believe that this drug can slow the disease. Researchers run a study. The study lasts 18 months. 1,800 Alzheimer’s patients help in the study. The study measures how a new drug works. The drug maybe can help with Alzheimer’s. The drug changes proteins in the brain. These proteins are important for the disease. Researchers are very excited. This drug is the first that can change the proteins. Sadly, the drug also makes serious new problems. Some patients have brain swelling or brain bleeding . Experts believe that careful watching will stop these problems. Difficult words: protein (a thing that makes the body work well), swell (to become larger or rounder), bleed (to lose blood from the body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Experts have evidence that animals can sense how we’re feeling and if we may be sick. According to a new study, dogs can distinguish the feelings of stress versus calm. Dogs have an incredible sense of smell. They have more than 200 million nerve endings inside the nose, compared to about 50 million for people. Dogs also have a larger part of the brain dedicated to sensing smells than humans; therefore, they’re able to detect odorants in a much lower concentration. Disease and illness change our overall smell which we emit through our breath and sweat. Dogs can sense if we’re happy or sad, and they have detected diseases including breast, lung, and cervical cancers. During the pandemic, they found the coronavirus. Difficult words: versus (in contrast to, against), odorant (a material that has a strong smell), cervical (the cervix or the lower part of the uterus). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A new study shows that dogs can tell if someone feels happy or stress. Dogs have a much better sense of smell than people. Dogs have more than 200 million nerve s in the nose, but people have only about 50 million. Dogs also have a larger part of the brain which senses smell. Some studies suggest that dogs know how we feel and when we are sick. We smell differently when we are sick or our emotions change, and dogs can easily recognize the change. Dogs can sense some types of cancer , and they also know if someone has the coronavirus. Difficult words: nerve (a brain part that helps you sense the world), recognize (to know who someone or what something is), cancer (a disease in which some of the parts of the body start to grow without control). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Dogs know how people feel. They know if someone is sick. A study explains these situations. Our bodies smell differently if we feel stress . Dogs have more than 200 million parts in the nose. The parts connect to their brain. People have only 50 million. Dogs’ brains are different, too. Dogs can smell much better than people. They can smell things which people cannot. Dogs can also detect some types of cancer . They know if someone has the coronavirus. We smell differently when we are sick. Dogs know very quickly when our smell changes. Difficult words: stress (worried and nervous), detect (to find something), cancer (some parts of the body start to grow without control). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Somalia’s healthcare system is overwhelmed and in crisis because of an increasing number of militant attacks and the worst drought in four decades. Hospitals have reported the number increased by 30% of mass casualty incidents from armed conflicts since 2021. At the end of October, 2022, militant group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for two car bomb blasts outside Somalia’s Ministry of Education. At least 120 people died, and it became the country’s deadliest incident in five years. Weeks later, hospitals are still dealing with the patient influx . However, a surge in violence is just one problem for the country. A regional hospital in Baidoa has reported a more than 170% rise in the number of malnourished children. The UN has warned that part of the country is on the brink of famine, and more than half a million children are at risk of death. Drought and conflicts displaced many of them. Difficult words: influx (an arrival of large numbers), malnourished (physically weak because of a lack of food), brink (a point at which something unpleasant is about to happen). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Since last year, violent attacks in Somalia increased. At the same time, the country is experiencing the worst drought in 40 years. Reports say that the number of attacks increased by 30% since last year, and hospitals are overwhelmed with patients. Recently, several deadly attacks also happened in big cities. Doctors tried to treat all patients, but more people were coming. Another problem is a high number of malnourished children. Dry weather led to less food for everyone. People move to areas where they can grow crops and to run away from danger. The UN said that more than 500,000 children could die from hunger and that some parts of Somalia are at risk of famine . Difficult words: drought (a long period of time without rain), malnourished (weak and without good food), at risk of famine (the time before many people don’t have enough food). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Somalia’s hospitals have a big problem. Too many patients are there. Many attacks happen in Somalia. Militant groups do the attacks. 30% more attacks happen than last year. The worst attack happens in October. Two bombs explode in cars. At least 120 people die. Hospitals are full. Many children are in hospitals, too. These children do not have enough good food. Recently, it rains too little in Somalia. People cannot grow crops . They move to places where they can grow crops. The UN says that more than 500,000 children in Somalia may die from hunger. Difficult words: patient (a person who is ill or hurt), militant group (a group of people who violently fight for changes in the country), crops (plants which people grow for food). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said that the country plans to have the world’s most powerful force. The announcement came after Kim inspected a test of the Hwasong-17 on November 18, 2022; it is North Korea’s largest intercontinental ballistic missile . He said that North Korea’s ultimate goal was to possess the most powerful strategic force, unprecedented in the century, to reliably protect the dignity and sovereignty of the government and people. Kim posed for pictures with scientists, engineers, and military officials who were involved in the test. Government media also showed his daughter, and her first appearance at the test implied she may become North Korea’s future leader. The missile can reach the US mainland, and the launch prompted the US to call for a UN Security Council to hold North Korea responsible for its missile tests, which are banned by UN resolutions. Difficult words: ballistic missile (a missile that is guided during takeoff but then travels freely and it falls to its target), dignity (honor or respect), sovereignty (the power of a country to control its own government). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Pictures showed him with scientists, engineers, and soldiers. His daughter was at the test, too, and many people speculated that she could become North Korea’s next leader. The rocket is called Hwasong-17, and it can reach the United States. The test alarmed US officials, who wanted to call for a meeting with the UN. Kim said that he wanted to protect North Korea and its people. He said that with the rocket, the country would become stronger than ever before. Difficult words: intercontinental (between continents), speculate (to speak about something without having enough information about it), alarm (to make someone feel frightened). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: test (to check how something works), ban (to stop officially), responsible (care about something and have control over it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Flossie is the world’s oldest cat; born in 1995, she is an impressive 27-years-old and now a Guinness World Record holder. Flossie had been living with other stray cats near Merseyside Hospital in the UK. One of the owners took pity on the kitten, and she took the cat in. 10 years later, the owner died, and a family member cared for her instead; she spent another 14 years with the second owner. Eventually, Flossie outlived her second owner too, and cats protection took over her care. People re-homed her to East London with her new owner Vicky who is the same age. Flossie is partially sighted , completely deaf, and has only three teeth left. However, she has a very healthy appetite, she likes to be stroked, and she’s very friendly and inquisitive . To beat the record for the oldest cat ever, Flossie still has years to go. Cream Puff reached 38 years old before she died in 2005. Difficult words: stray (lost or separated from the others), sighted (able to see), inquisitive (interested in learning things). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Flossie the cat is 27 years old, which makes her the oldest cat in the world. Flossie was born in 1995, and she lived with other stray cats in Merseyside, UK. One woman felt sorry for the cat, so she took her home. 10 years later, the owner died, and Flossie moved in with another member of the family. 14 years later, the new owner died, too, and Flossie went to cats protection, where people look after cats. These people knew how to care for old cats. Recently, Vicky from East London adopted Flossie, and she didn’t even know that she was the oldest cat in the world. The cat is deaf , she can’t see well, and she has only three teeth. She still has a healthy appetite , she is friendly, and she likes to learn new things. Difficult words: stray (lost or alone), deaf (not able to hear anything), appetite (a feeling that you want to eat food). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Thousands of cosplayers and anime fans flocked to the annual Anime Festival Asia (AFA) in Singapore; people held the festival for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic. AFA began in 2008, and it’s the largest and most followed Japanese pop culture event in Southeast Asia. Anime is a sub-culture from Japan, which has continued to thrive and grow internationally in recent years, due to its vast online presence and supportive participants. In 2019, the three-day convention attracted 120,000 attendees, and organizers expect to reach at least the same numbers for this year. For many cosplayers, the event feels like a meeting of old friends because they are in constant online contact with each other. Difficult words: cosplayer (a person who dresses up as a fictional character), pop culture (music, TV, cinema, books, and other media that are popular and enjoyed by many people), sub-culture (ideas, art, and a way of life of a group of people within a society). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last weekend, the Anime Festival Asia happened in Singapore. Cosplayers and fans of anime from all of Southeast Asia could finally meet after two years of COVID-19 rules and laws. The festival started in 2008, and since that time it became popular all over the world. Anime comes from Japan, but many anime events now happen outside of Asia. Cosplayers like to dress up as their favorite anime characters, and they often enjoy the music from Japanese anime movies. The pandemic didn’t badly impact the event because fans met online during that time. In 2019, the three-day event welcomed 120,000 visitors, and organizers expect that this year’s number will be the same or even higher. Difficult words: cosplay er (a person who wears a costume of a fictional character), anime (a style of animation which uses colorful images and characters can have large eyes), dress up (to put on unusual, fancy, or formal clothes for a special event). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: animation (films or computer games using drawings), character (a person in a book or film), organizer (a person who leads an event or activity). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The UK’s top judges have ended Scotland’s attempt for a second independence referendum. The Supreme Court ruled unanimously that a vote would need to be approved by the UK government, as in 2014 when Scotland held its previous referendum. Nationalist leader Nicola Sturgeon said that the government denied her nation a democratic right after Scotland voted against Brexit and her Scottish National Party triumphed in subsequent elections. Sturgeon added that the court ruling showed that the UK wasn’t a voluntary partnership, and she vowed to get a legal referendum. For Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, the decision was a relief, as he tries to restore investor confidence in the country. Like his predecessors , Sunak said that he wouldn’t give permission for another referendum on Scotland’s three-centuries-old union with England and Wales. Difficult words: unanimously (agreed to by all), triumph (a great victory or achievement), predecessor (a person who held a job or office before the current holder). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

UK’s Supreme Court rejected Scotland’s attempt for a referendum on its independence. The court said that if Scotland wanted a referendum, the UK government would have to agree. Nicola Sturgeon, Scotland’s First Minister and leader of the Scottish National Party, said that Scotland voted against Brexit, and Scottish people had the right to another referendum. UK Prime Minister Rishi Sunak said that he wouldn’t agree with another referendum. He said that he didn’t want to break the union of England, Scotland, and Wales that is three hundred years old. Sunak was happy about the court’s decision because his country is in crisis, and the referendum would worsen the situation. Difficult words: reject (to say no), referendum (a vote in which all the people in a country or area vote to change someone), union (a group of things together). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: referendum (when all the people of a country vote to change something), independence (not under control of someone or something else), prime minister (the leader of a type of a government with several parts). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Bullfighters in France fear that the government will ban their art across the country. The Spanish custom is still allowed in several southern France cities; however, the lawmakers want to ban it, and 75% of the French support the decision. The custom is known as Corrida; it involves a bullfight with the matador in a shining costume who usually kills the animal with a sword thrust . For supporters, this age-old tradition must be preserved because the south of France is an important stronghold for bullfights. For critics, Corrida is a cruel ritual that has no place in modern society. Difficult words: thrust (to push suddenly with force), stronghold (a place that is a center for particular activity or belief). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The French government is planning to ban bullfighting in the country, and 75% of people agree with this ban. The Spanish custom known as Corrida is very popular in southern France. Matadors say that it is a part of the life in the area and a tradition which people must keep alive. Bullfighting is business which matadors want to continue. For critics, Corrida is cruel, and it shouldn’t happen in modern society . In a bullfight, a matador in a shining costume usually kills a bull with a sword. The fight is dangerous for the matador, too, but the animal almost always dies. Difficult words: custom (something that people usually do), matador (a person who fights with a bull in a bullfight), society (people who live together in groups or communities). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Despite Kyiv’s blackout, doctors in Ukraine performed open-heart surgery on a 14-year-old boy. Russian missiles rained down on the Ukrainian capital city on Wednesday when the Kyiv Heart Institute unexpectedly lost light, power, and water. Hospital staff jumped into action and started a backup generator to keep the support system running. The surgeons continued to operate, using only the lights from their phones and headlamps. Despite the difficulties, the surgery was successful, and the patient’s prognosis was good. The blackout happened amid heavy Russian bombardment in Ukraine that cut electricity and water across the capital and other parts of the country. Since October, Russia has openly acknowledged it is targeting Ukraine’s civil power and heat systems with long-range missiles and drones. The goal is to reduce the country’s ability to fight and push it to negotiate. Difficult words: prognosis (a doctor’s opinion on the expected development of a condition or disease), bombardment (a continuous attack with bombs and other missiles), acknowledge (to admit). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last Wednesday, Russian missiles hit the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv. It happened just at the moment when doctors were doing an open-heart surgery on a 14-year-old boy. Doctors were in the surgery when suddenly the lights started to flicker and the room went dark. Hospital staff quickly started a generator to get some electricity. The doctors couldn’t wait for more light, so they continued to work on the operation with only the light from their phones and headlamps. Luckily, the boy survived and he was doing well after the operation. Russia admitted that it wanted to cut Kyiv off from electricity and water. The idea was to stop Ukraine’s fight and to negotiate with Russia. Difficult words: flicker (to go on and off quickly), generator (a machine which makes electricity), negotiate (to deal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: operation (medical work inside the body), generator (a machine which makes electricity), infrastructure (buildings, roads, and power supplies). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Cristiano Ronaldo left Manchester United by mutual agreement with immediate effect, as he said the time is right to seek a new challenge. Recently, the club and he have been embroiled in a legal battle. The club suspended the 37-year-old player when Ronaldo refused to come off the bench last month, and then, he gave a TV interview about his frustrations. He explained he felt betrayed , and he had no respect for the club’s manager Ten Hag, who largely used him as a substitute. Last month, Ronaldo refused to go onto the pitch against Tottenham Hotspur, and he walked down the tunnel with minutes of the match to play. Following years of protests from fans, Manchester United’s owners are considering selling the club. The Glazers bought the club in 2005 for 790 million pounds; however, Manchester United hasn’t won a Premier League Title since 2013, and the team struggled to find a long-term manager after Sir Alex Ferguson retired. Multiple protests have happened in recent years, and some games had to be postponed because of them. If someone else buys Manchester United, the expectation is it will go to US investors. Difficult words: mutual (shared between two or more people or groups), embroil (to involve in an argument or difficult situation), betray (to be false or disloyal to someone). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Cristiano Ronaldo is leaving Manchester United. The player announced the news on social media, and he said that it was time for a life change. In a TV interview, he said that he felt the club betrayed him, and that he didn’t respect the club’s manager Ten Hag. Manchester United last won the Premier League in 2013, and the team couldn’t find a good manager. Many fans protested in recent years, and the protests delayed some matches. The club owners are considering if they will sell the club, probably to US buyers. Difficult words: substitute (a player who replaces another player during a match), betray (to be false or unfair to someone), delay (to make something happen later). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
